question: Does year-over-year card-spend growth for a ticker's brands, measured before the report, predict the next reported revenue growth beyond a seasonal public baseline?
mechanism: Card transactions are executed consumer demand, observable weekly/monthly before quarterly disclosure. If consensus is slow to incorporate transaction-level demand, spend growth leads reported revenue growth and post-report drift.
falsification: No stable improvement over the primary baseline on the design partition (2015-2018 check; CA0056 history starts 2019, so the design claim rests on CA0031/CA0028 historic card panels or is explicitly restricted)
Apparent effect disappears when the panel's monthly reweighting is lagged past the revision window
Apparent effect is explained by covered-vs-uncovered composition (panel membership predicts the result)
Effect vanishes when ranked within sector (it was a consumer-sector bet)
Bridge to 20-day excess returns is negative after costs even if revenue prediction improves
